description: Make `you submit` success output actionable for humans and scripts by extending the submit API response with work identifiers, shaping human and `--json` CLI output (including verify hints), clarifying error surfaces, and documenting the submit → verify loop in packaged docs.

context.customerAsk: After `you submit`, operators and agents need the created work id, name, and work type—not only a trace id—plus a suggested `you work show` or `you work list` command. Scripts need a stable `--json` object. Errors should distinguish unreachable factory vs API rejection.
context.problem: `you submit` prints `Submitted work: <traceId>` on success and the OpenAPI `SubmitWorkResponse` only requires `traceId`, forcing immediate `you work list` and causing duplicate submits during agent-driven docs work.
context.solution: Extend `SubmitWorkResponse` with normalized work metadata from the submit handler, map it in `pkg/cli/submit` to human lines and a stable `--json` envelope (including `endpointPath` and `sessionId`), improve bounded error text, and document the contract and verify loop in `you docs work` aligned with work-inspection commands.

acceptanceCriteria: HTTP 201 submit responses expose workId, name, and workTypeName (and sessionId for session-scoped routes) via OpenAPI and handlers using existing normalization rules.
Human-mode `you submit` prints name, workTypeName, traceId, workId when available, and a one-line `you work show` or `you work list --name` hint without dumping full payloads.
Global `--json` success emits one object with workId, name, workTypeName, traceId, sessionId, and endpointPath; exit code 0.
Submit failures never print success output; transport errors are distinguishable from HTTP API errors with bounded body summaries.
Packaged `you docs work` documents human and JSON success shapes plus the submit → verify command loop.
Targeted CLI and API tests prove success and failure output behavior with mocked HTTP.
Quality gate: backend typecheck, lint, and relevant tests pass before merge.

userStories.title: Submit API returns work identifiers on 201
userStories.description: As an API consumer, I need SubmitWorkResponse to include accepted work identifiers so clients do not guess after a successful submit.
acceptanceCriteria: OpenAPI SubmitWorkResponse includes workId, name, workTypeName, and traceId; session-scoped routes also return sessionId matching the path.
pkg/api submit handlers populate fields from the same WorkRequest normalization that assigns stable work ids before returning HTTP 201.
API tests assert the success JSON body for default and session-scoped submit.
Generated Go and UI OpenAPI types compile after regeneration.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Human success output for you submit
userStories.description: As an operator, I want submit stdout to show what was accepted and which work command to run next so I can verify without listing the entire factory.
acceptanceCriteria: On HTTP 201, stdout includes name, workTypeName, traceId, and workId when the API returns workId.
Stdout prints you work show <work-id> when workId is present; otherwise you work list --name <name> with explicit fallback wording.
Stdout does not print the full HTTP response or request payload; verbose diagnostics remain stderr-only.
CLI httptest covers human stdout and hint selection for responses with and without workId.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: JSON success output for you submit --json
userStories.description: As a script, I want a single parseable JSON confirmation object after submit so I can automate verify steps without scraping text.
acceptanceCriteria: Global --json success writes one JSON object with keys workId, name, workTypeName, traceId, sessionId, and endpointPath.
Exit code is 0 on success; stdout contains only that JSON object.
CLI test asserts JSON field presence and values from a mocked 201 response including a session-scoped endpointPath.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Clear submit error surfaces
userStories.description: As an agent, I want submit failures to be clearly classified so I do not treat transport or API errors as successful enqueue.
acceptanceCriteria: Connection and transport failures report the factory URL as unreachable and emit no success line.
Non-201 HTTP responses return an error including status and a bounded API message or body snippet.
When error JSON includes workId, the CLI error text includes it in a stable workId= form.
CLI tests cover unreachable server, structured 400 ErrorResponse, and non-JSON error bodies.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Document submit output and verify loop
userStories.description: As an agent author, I want you docs work to describe submit success output and the verify commands that follow.
acceptanceCriteria: you docs work documents human success fields, --json keys, and example success objects.
The same section documents verify with you work show and you work list --name / --work-type-name aligned with work-inspection behavior.
Docs state diagnostics stay on stderr and payloads are not echoed on success.
